fi-rhinecanthus-aculeatus.title: Humu Humu Picasso Triggerfish
rows: About 10 in; wild record 30 cm (11.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Squid, krill, clams, small fish and hard-shelled shrimp to wear down its teeth
Indo-Pacific: East Africa eastward through northern Australia to Hawaiian, Marquesas and Tuamotu islands, north to southern Japan

fi-xanthichthys-auromarginatus.title: Blue Throat Triggerfish
fi-xanthichthys-auromarginatus.summary: One of the calmer triggers: grey-brown with pale blue spots and yellow-edged fins; males have a blue throat patch. It swims up in the water to feed on plankton.
rows: About 12 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 30 cm (11.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: mysis shrimp, fortified brine shrimp, krill, squid, chopped fish, clam flesh, hard-shelled marine foods, carnivore pellets
Indo-Pacific: Mauritius eastward through northern Australia to the Hawaiian and Society islands, north to southern Japan
notes: Usually ignores corals, but ornamental shrimp, hermit crabs, snails and urchins are at risk.

fi-sufflamen-bursa.title: Bursa Triggerfish (Boomerang Trigger)
fi-sufflamen-bursa.summary: A tan-and-white triggerfish from the Indo-Pacific with two curved, boomerang-shaped bands behind the eye that darken or fade with mood. A tough, aggressive fish for a fish-only tank.
rows: About 10 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 25 cm (9.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: chopped marine fish, shrimp, squid, clam flesh, frozen carnivore preparations, hard-shelled foods, spirulina-enriched foods
Indo-Pacific: East Africa eastward through northern Australia to Hawaiian, Marquesas and Pitcairn islands, north to south Japan
notes: Keep with robust fish of equal or larger size; it nips slow fish such as lionfish and eats shrimp, crabs, snails and urchins.

fi-melichthys-indicus.title: Indian Triggerfish
fi-melichthys-indicus.summary: A black triggerfish with pale streaks at the base of its fins and white bands running from the eyes, from Indian Ocean reefs. Adults hide only to sleep or when startled.
rows: About 9 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 25 cm (9.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Omnivore: benthic invertebrates such as crustaceans, worms and urchins, plus some seaweed
Indian Ocean: Red Sea and East Africa eastward to western Thailand and Indonesia
notes: Keep with fish of similar size and temperament.
warn: Not reef safe; it eats invertebrates.

fi-melichthys-vidua.title: Pinktail Triggerfish
fi-melichthys-vidua.summary: A handsome trigger with an emerald-green body, yellow touches on the face and fins, and a bright pink tail, from Indo-Pacific seaward reefs.
rows: About 14 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 40 cm (15.7 in) TL (FishBase)
If keeping more than one, add one male and several females together
Varied meaty diet such as squid, krill, clam, small fish and hard-shelled shrimp (wears down its ever-growing teeth)
Indo-Pacific: East Africa eastward through northern Australia to Hawaiian and Tuamotu islands, north to southern Japan
notes: Strong jaws: it can chew through tank equipment.
warn: Eats crustaceans and small fish; only with caution in a reef.
